note: No vulnerable-instrumentation.patch was present for this sample, so bindings were reconstructed from ground_truth.json's fine_trace/root_cause_criterion, which quote literal lines from the actual vulnerable src/http.c (getchunk and deliver_chunked_chunks), cross-checked against patch.diff's unified diff (which shows the surrounding unchanged getchunk body -- 'size_t i = 0, n;', 'n = mg_unhexn(s.ptr, i);', 'if (s.len < i + n + 4) return false;' -- only the while-loop condition itself is replaced by the fix) and assertion_results.json's numeric matrix (vulnerable: prefix_len/prefix_scan.prefix_len/unhexn_result.prefix_len=93, n/unhexn_result.n=18446744073709551614, s_len=380, memmove_sink.dl=18446744073709551614, all matching fine_trace's stated values). 'i' (declared 'size_t i = 0, n;' at http.c:961) is the prefix-scan cursor/length used both right after the scan loop (prefix_scan.prefix_len) and as the second argument to mg_unhexn(s.ptr, i) at http.c:962 (unhexn_result.prefix_len) -- same variable, two checkpoints, per the a_prefix_len_feeds_unhexn transition asserting they're equal. 'n' is the mg_unhexn(...) return value assigned at http.c:962, read again at the guard check http.c:964 ('if (s.len < i + n + 4) return false;', bare 'n' field of the observed a_n_exceeds_buffer assertion) and unchanged through to *datalen = n at http.c:968 (unhexn_result.n). 's_len' is 's.len', the len member of the struct mg_str s parameter to getchunk, read in that same guard check. 'memmove_sink.dl' is 'dl', the literal third argument to memmove(p + processed, buf + ofs + pl, dl) at src/http.c:997 in deliver_chunked_chunks (ground_truth.json fine_trace step 5 / verified_invariants.json node n_sink_memmove_uses_overflowed_dl), a function the patch does not touch, so the variable name is unchanged between vulnerable and fixed versions. 'hex_prefix_len' (from a_root_hex_validation) intentionally omitted: it names a synthetic/behavioral quantity -- 'how many leading bytes of the prefix are actually hex digits' -- that Stage 04's validator computed only for comparison purposes; the vulnerable source has no such digit-counting expression at all (that absence is precisely the root cause, r_missing_hex_digit_validation), so no real vulnerable-version source expression exists to bind it to. It falls back to build_probes.py's field-name-disclosure path instead of a fabricated binding.
